Theme

# Philosophy quotes about choice

Choice is the hinge of agency: selecting among options under reasons, constraints, and uncertainty.

15 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Free will, decision theory, and existential choice all ask how choosing is possible and what makes a choice one’s own.

## In the history of philosophy

Aristotelian prohairesis, Stoic assent, existential commitment, and modern behavioral science offer overlapping vocabularies.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Aristotle](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/aristotle) , [Friedrich Nietzsche](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/friedrich-nietzsche) , [Søren Kierkegaard](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/soren-kierkegaard) , [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-paul-sartre) , [Hannah Arendt](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/hannah-arendt) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [Dante Alighieri](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/dante-alighieri) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is choice in philosophy?

It is the act of selecting among alternatives, often tied to responsibility and practical reason.

### Are we free to choose?

Compatibilists, libertarians, and determinists disagree; many still affirm practical responsibility.

### Where are philosophy quotes about choice?

See this theme alongside freedom, action, and responsibility.
